text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles [[VIDEOID:886df78722d87a8bdca79a9702180ce2]] This set is awesome!! There are a couple things to note about it that could be potential downsides/issues, if not prepared for-- but otherwise, everything is great! Below I will group the main points and for the 3 potential issues I'll mark it with this symbol:🔴 to hopefully make it easier to read through!

•We received all pieces included, and boxing, in great condition.

•1 car is included

•The quality of materials are true to Hot Wheels- great and sturdy plastic.

•It's a fairly easy set-up. My 9 year old put it together on her own by reading through the instructions step-by-step. It took around 30 minutes, may have been quicker but she often took short pauses, though she didn't need any help.

•There are about 3 different configurations you can do with this set. The video I posted shows each of these.

•Can connect to other Hot Wheels tracks and sets. (Including the colossal crash set that can be seen some in the background of the video I posted)

•Does not require batteries

•There are no levers that need to be reset for cars to go through the loops- my daughter has other loop sets that have those.

•You can set it up so that the launcher connects and starts at any of the loops. For example- you can connect the launcher to just the middle loop and the smallest. You can also try to launch it opposite- starting at the smallest loop and ending with the largest.

•You don't have to use the jumping ramps…you can have the cars finish the loops on a flat track.

🔴 One of the potential issues is the launcher- maybe it's just our launcher, or how we use it, but it can be a bit tricky to hit it with the right amount of pressure. Too hard and it knocks it off track. Too soft and it won't go around the loop. Sometimes it can take many tries and others it works right away. We have a few other types of launchers-- the long white one that is shown in the video I posted is the one she prefers to use since it seems to work better. Not everyone will have extra launchers, though. My daughter usually has no problem with trying multiple times with the one included in the set but I figured it's worth noting that it may not be a perfect launch each time.

🔴 The other possible issue are the cars used with it. You'll likely want at least a handful of different types of cars on hand, just in case. The one included does work pretty good. My daughter has a decent sized collection of cars and there a quite a few that often don't make it through the biggest loop. This could either be the car itself that doesn't work well or could also be an issue of the launcher (as just mentioned above). Some of her cars struggle on the biggest loop with the launcher provided- but when connected to the "stronger" launcher, they do great. And there's a few that still just don't make it. This could be an issue if this were very first set for a kiddo and if they have only 1 or 2 cars…just something to keep in mind if considering purchasing this set, you may want to consider also purchasing a handful of cars so that they can get the most use from it.

🔴 When you have it set-up as the Daredevil Jump or Gravity Drop, it sort of seems like the track isn't long enough since the cars shoot further past the cup a lot. So we added extra tracks (which aren't included in this set) and it helped a lot…the cars land in the cup more times than not. At the very end of the video I posted, you can see how we added an extra track to the Daredevil Jump set-up.

All-in-all: We love it! It keeps my 9 year old busy-- even if she doesn't connect it to her other tracks. She likes trying to get the cars in the cup and thinks that the triple loop feature is awesome.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles

Some of the ad pages in the 43172 building instructions are different, but the models are the same.

The Elsa’s Magical Castle model isn’t large, but it has loads of sparkle and detail; and tons of play potential in the many accessories (e,g., castle furniture, Olaf’s train) and moving parts (e,g., swirling staircase, snow slide). It’s one of my all-time favorite LEGO buildings--one that I have on permanent display (alongside my big Disney castle model).

What I love most about Elsa’s castle is that it incorporates a lot of transparent “Frozen blue” bricks, many of which have embedded silver sparkles. I love shiny stuff, and Elsa’s shimmering cape is something to behold. I also love trains, so Olaf’s train is another plus. The little snowmen’s teeter-totter (near the snow fort) is fun. I don’t really care for the scary snow monster, but it helps in reenacting scenes from the movie.

Some of the model’s sparkle is added with stickers, but there aren’t a lot of stickers, and they’re easy to apply. There is a moving slide that opens and closes the tall castle front doors. There is a spiral staircase that swirls open when you turn a knob. The figures of Elsa and Anna are true to the cartoon figures in the Frozen film. This is truly a great, classic LEGO set, based on a great, classic Disney movie.

Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll, Blonde Baby Alive is an iconic doll. She was one of the first dolls that not only took a bottle, but also ate food, mixed and served to her from premade packets. She has been available in many different versions, each with the same eat/drink concept with a slightly different variation. My Baby All Gone is one of the latest Baby Alive dolls and she will easily keep your little one serving, feeding, changing, and burping her baby for hours.

What sets this Baby Alive doll apart from most of the others in the series is her ability to say so many different things. She still takes a bottle, eats food, pees, and poops just like the other Baby Alive dolls, but for a more realistic twist, she makes periodic statements from her wee little mouth. She will say that she wants to cuddle, that she just went pee, and so on. Her baby- ish voice and cute sayings will appeal strongly to young girls still going through their mommy phase.

My girls are both in their early years of elementary school, but they still like dolls and they like Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll just as much if not more than the others in the series, of which they have quite a few dolls. What they like best is the feature that sets this doll apart: The sayings, mentioned above. They like that she says so many different things- more than 30 sayings in all- because it makes her seem more real. I agree that the multitude of sayings is a vast improvement on other dolls that, while they might speak, say only three or four different things. My girls like playing the role of mommy, changing diapers, giving Baby Alive a nap, and everything else that goes with being a mom.

The one disadvantage of this Baby Alive doll is the same disadvantage with the others- you have to constantly purchase refill packs. Trust me, the few packs of food and the small number of diapers will not last long at all! In a matter of a day or two out of the package, your girls will be asking for replacement food and diapers. We have had this doll in our household for only about 10 days and have already ordered a refill pack.

Little girls often like to play the role of a mommy and Baby Alive is one of the best dolls for interactive mommy play. My girls like her very much and I like that they are happy. The cost of the refill packs can add up, so try to improvise when you can or create your own cloth diapers that can be washed and reused. Then watch as the young girl in your household practices her mommy role with a doll that, while not alive, is about as close as you can get to the real thing.
text_fidelity_b: Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll, Blonde

Paint & Decorate Your Own Coin Bank with Color Changing Sequin Decal & Metallic Holographic Paints, Blue Spoiler alert: what a fun group art project for a small group of children (or children at heart lol)! Great for siblings, sleepovers, or homeschoolers trying to squeeze in a fun extracurricular class :)

I have three girls ranging in ages 6 through almost 11, and ALL three of them enjoyed doing this project together (well, four if you include mom lol). The quality of the tea set itself is the real deal: ceramic, and with proper (and of course gentle) care, this set should last long after the paint has cured (one page of simple--but important--instructions is included that tell you how to properly cure the paint after it has dried.)

Something I should point out to save some frustration: please realize that the unpainted ceramic arrives in a somewhat glossy finish... so that, when painted, the final finish will appear less like the picture of the tea set on the box, and more like an abstract watercolor design. Just something to keep in mind :)

Also, be sure to allow 24 hours for the paint to dry before curing it. Otherwise the color might appear weak. After completely dry, cure in the oven according to the included instructions. Allow to COOL COMPLETELY (preferably safely out of reach) and finally after a bit of patience...

VOILA! A lovely, top quality, and yes even CUSTOM tea set that may be enjoyed over and over again (my girls have already enjoyed several tea parties). A giftable winner!!

Insect Lore - Butterfly Growing Kit - Butterfly Habitat Kit with Voucher to Redeem 5 Caterpillars, STEM Journal, Butterfly Feeder & More – Life Science & STEM Education – Butterfly Science Kit The Live Butterfly Garden by Insect Lore is a fun, hands- on educational experience that is certain to appeal to even the most stubborn, disinterested child. With the Live Butterfly Garden, children get to observe the process of metamorphosis, right before their eyes. Starting with caterpillars, children watch the little critters eat food, create a cocoon, and then transform into fully grown adult butterflies. The butterflies can then be observed in their habitat for a while before setting free.

This butterfly garden is great for dozens of reasons, the most obvious of which is the educational value. Reading about insects and metamorphosis is one thing, but seeing the process live is another thing entirely. Kids get to learn how caterpillars/butterflies live, eat, and thrive; how to care for them; etc. They get to observe the caterpillars and butterflies at play and watch the butterflies eat their food, which is provided in the package. The caterpillars that come with the Live Butterfly Garden are painted ladies, which are not very common and will not be recognized by most children. However, most kids won't care- the fun of watching these small caterpillars transform into butterflies will have many kids gazing in awe, and prompt them to ask many questions.

This educational toy is a huge hit and my kids loved it, but there were a few small issues. One was waiting for the caterpillars to arrive in the mail. To get the caterpillars, you have to mail in an included certificate, along with a check, and then wait. It seems like an eternity, especially from the perspective of young children, and it took longer than expected. Anther problem was parting with the butterflies. Once you have the caterpillars and they have transformed into adult butterflies, the next problem will be setting them free. Kids will grow attached to their small, winged friends and will not want to let them go. Another minor issue is with the transferring of the caterpillars from their small container- the one you receive in the mail- into the actual habitat. The container that the caterpillars arrive in has a paper area at the top, where the caterpillars will hang as they spin their cocoons. This paper section is fairly easy to remove, but the problem is that the cocoons are very delicately attached, and that means that some will fall off when the transfer is made. You will need to pin this piece of paper to the inside of the butterfly garden, but the kit doesn't include any pins. Safety pins or straight pins work, and it would have been nice if these were included in the kit.

Still, when all factors are considered, the Live Butterfly Garden is worth the purchase and young children will enjoy the educational experience. Sure, it could be improved a little bit by making a few minor changes, but this is still a very good toy and considering my kid's fascination with the process, along with the educational value, it earns an easy recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Insect Lore - Butterfly Growing Kit - Butterfly Habitat Kit with Voucher to Redeem 5 Caterpillars, STEM Journal, Butterfly Feeder & More – Life Science & STEM Education – Butterfly Science Kit

ENJBRICK Harry Castle Potter Toy Building Set,Compatible with Lego Idea Building Blocks Kit for Kids and Adults 521pcs This set consists of thirteen #1 bags for Weasley's Wizarding Wheezes (the purple and orange building), eight #2 bags for Flourish and Blotts (the green and brown building), one bag of plates, instructions, and a small sticker sheet.

The bags are not numbered individually. Trust me, open all the bags for a building. So all #1 bags or all #2 bags. You’ll need a lot of space for the pieces, but it’s less frustrating in the long run. Steps require pieces from every bag as you go. Finding the pieces for each step took the longest part of this build.

The instructions are mostly clear*, but the build experience itself is frustrating. Some pieces stay together and some do not. I spent so much time rebuilding because a section would break when I put new pieces on. For example, the window section for WWW, I had to test window pieces to see which would stay together and then stay on the building. For the upper window section, where the arms come out, I had to redo that three or four times, carefully holding the windows together.

*Step 64 has the wrong pieces, there is a sheet to show the proper pieces.

The buildings are delicate. On my Flourish and Blotts building, the bottom barely stays together, so I can’t take it off the base. The buildings are hollow inside, so you can hide items. The F&B building has a tray inside, and the WWW building has a rod to use to pop the tray out. If I popped the tray out, I’d have to put the F&B building back together. I don’t care for the hiding space, I’d prefer buildings that were more stable, especially if they’re supposed to be bookends.

Some of the stickers go over multiple pieces, one sticker on 2 or 3 pieces. The Dark Mark sticker is misspelled: DRRK MRRK.

Overall, the finished set looks good, but getting to that finished set was a somewhat frustrating experience.

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

The packaging indicated Callie is from Japan, and she definitely has more almond-shaped eyes than Meredith. Her light skin, brown hair (instead of black), and eye shape reminded my bi-racial girls of themselves. That is the true gift of doll lines that have unique face sculpts, to provide a mirror so all little girls can have a doll that resembles them, as well as a truly diverse line of dolls.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie

text_fidelity_a:
Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min I'd never heard of Similo before, but there are other varieties of this card game(History and Myths...in June, at least). They can even be mixed with this one for a different game and there are instructions for doing so in this deck. The game is pretty simple. There's a Clue Giver and the other players are Guessers. The Clue Giver picks one of the characters in the deck(putting it back afterwards, along with 11 other cards) and then uses only cards leftover to give clues(5 cards in hand at a time), with no words or gestures. The 12 cards for the Guessers are spread in a grid and the Clue Giver gives one card per round for a clue. Vertical means there's something similar to the Secret Character and horizontal means there's something different. For example, if I'm the Clue Giver and I picked Aladdin, I could put Genie vertically, since they're from the same tale or I could put Cheshire Cat horizontally, since Aladdin isn't an animal. It's up the the Clue Giver to decide what's similar or different. The game is over within 5 rounds. The Guessers take away one card for the first round, two for the second, etc. If the Secret Character is taken away, the game is over, but if the final card is the Secret Character, the Guessers win.

I like that this game is cooperative. My children have to work together to win the game. We have plenty of competitive games, but very few cooperative ones, so this is a nice feature for us. I also like the illustrations on the cards. They're brightly colored and well done. It also doesn't take long to play, so if short on time, it's a nice way to pass just a bit of time and still have fun.
text_fidelity_b: Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) Mattel has brought a new world to target practice and just plain fun with soft dart guns with this BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster. With no batteries required, the fun is endless. Instead of batteries to power the gun, it is air powered. You have to pump the gun to get enough air pressure to fire the soft darts. Mattel states the gun is for ages 6 and up, but this gun is on the heavy side and requires a bit of strength just to pump it, so I feel ages 7 and up would be a better fit. Even though our 6 year old neighbor didn't want to put this gun down, it was difficult for him to pump it for firing.

The gun is very sturdy being large and made of a heavy plastic. I can see this gun lasting quite a bit of use and not ending up in the trash for a long while. Once pumped it is easy to fire, whether firing one dart or the entire 20 dart clip. At the end of the gun is a special shield you can open up to not only protect yourself from oncoming darts, but your opponents darts will actually stick to this protective shield, allowing you to capture his darts.

Besides the gun there are 30 Smart Stick darts, a 20 dart clip and a Smart Stick target included. The target is great for improving your aim, especially firing one dart at a time. The 20 dart clip is really fun, whether firing at the target or your opponent, as it fires all 20 darts in a matter of a few seconds. It literally fires up to 50 feet, as we shot all 20 darts and several darts went well over 45 feet away. The rapid fire at such a distance is really a lot of fun for the backyard.

Even though these darts are really soft plastic, you will find out that once the children find out how much fun it is to shoot darts at both the target and each other, you may want to purchase the safety eye gear. I don't know if having all 20 darts coming at you from 50 feet away would need some type of eye protection, but I feel it's better to have some type of eye gear on. There is no doubt, this is a safe, sturdy toy with your children wanting to run around and play with this outdoors, gives it 5 Stars. Just getting the kids off the couch away from video games makes it a 5 Star toy, as the exercise alone is worth 5 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset I usually write a review and sometimes include pros and cons, but for this item, I'm going to let the pros and cons stand almost on their own.

Pros:
- Large for the MSRP of $15 (measures 23" by 19" by 7" high)
- Simple, fun play
- Kid-powered, no batteries required
- Interesting challenge
- Unique play style for Hot Wheels with "drifting" action
- A lot of pieces in the box (12 with car)
- Can interact a little with Hot Wheels track builder track by attaching
to load a car
- Can load multiple cars (other cars not included) in line to get shot
out of the launcher one at a time
- Added play options of hitting the included flags or knocking off cars
(not included) perched at the top 3 points
- Relatively quiet play
- Perforated package back makes opening easy (this is standard to modern
Hot Wheels packaging)

Neutral thoughts:
- Not super easy to put together, but not that hard
- 6 stickers, not too many, all easy to apply
- Assembled playset segments don't sit as flush against each other,
which makes precision drifting more difficult than it should be, but
it's not that noticeable unless you're picky

Cons:
- Doesn't disassemble for storage (moreso than most of these things)
- No other way to interact with Track Builder track sections beyond loading a car, so it has to be the final part of any setup
- Parts don't have instruction's letters stamped or painted on them

It's a fun toy with few downsides, a good value and can be used with other cars. The included car is non-exclusive, but that's no big deal considering the price of the set. The action is not truly "drifting" which would be impossible with a Hot Wheels car, but it imitates drifting well via a launcher sliding the car sideways with the back facing out around the playset track. Superfight: Core Deck - A Card Game of Absurd Arguments | Fun Family Friendly, Party Game of Super Powers and Super Problems, Enjoyed by Kids, Teens, and Adults, 500-Card Deck, 3+ Players, Ages 8+ We got this as a group game to play Memorial Day weekend and while we did not follow the directions (we made up our own - see below) - it was amazingly fun! We played late into the night and still talk about some of the awesome and amazing combos! (it's hard to beat three Jason's made of lava - even if you have the hummus the card). So much laughter and I look forward to playing it anytime I can!

For those interested on how we played as a large group: we divided up into teams of two or three. Each team got one white (character) card and two black (attribute) cards. They had a minute or so to talk about strategy amongst themselves. Then - the SuperFight was on! We went around the group and each team got to tell everyone about their character (& abilities) and then debate with each other on why they would win. Everyone as a group agreed or disagreed depending on the strength of the debate. We didn't keep score, but just round by round. Lots of fun and easy to play anywhere!

Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model I bought this model for my 7 year old grandson who recently started riding and currently aspires to be a Vet. The model is small and some of the bits are tiny but manageable if one has reasonable dexterity. It is not for the easily frustrated as it requires patience and a thought to put together. The documentation is marginally helpful, and we used the picture on the cover more that we did the provided sheet for guidance. I also bought "Horse Anatomy (Dover Nature Coloring Book)" which proved a useful addition.
I worked with my grandson to put the model together for the first time. One of the small pieces had molding flash still attached which prevented it from fitting properly until the excess material was removed. The pieces will all fit together properly, but the final assembly is not terribly robust.
To reiterate, it was a bit of a problem solving exercise to fit the pieces into the correct spots, but we found the feeling of accomplishment worth the effort. I do not recommend this as a quick-assembly toy. There are better choices for that purpose. However, I do recommend it as a learning exercise for the curious child. It was fun to see my grandson made associations with his dog and human anatomy during the process. The finished product is suitable for display in a safe spot and can be disassembled and reassembled as long as one keeps track of all the pieces (you wouldn't want to lose his pancreas, would you?). I deducted a star for the less than great documentation.
text_fidelity_b: Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model

Evviva Ant Habitat W/LED Light. Enjoy A Magnificent Habitat. Great for Kids & Adults. Evviva Ant Ecosystem W/Enhanced Blue Gel. Educational & Learning Science Kit. Live Ants Not Included This ant farm was a fascinating gift for everyone, not just the 6 year old who got it. We ordered the ants from AntsAlive .com and when they arrived they quickly scurried about, digging their first hole within a few hours. Before you add the ants, you must poke 3 to 4 holes in the gel to help the ants get started. I’m wondering if the negative reviews forgot this step, leaving the ants confused in the farm on where they could go.

I highly recommend refrigerating the ants for 10 minutes before you add them to the farm so they don’t immediately escape. I also highly recommend putting them in on the side nearest the white air hole plug. Inevitably a few ants will have died in shipment and it’s much easier to remove them through the hole then removing the entire lid (as others will try to escape).

Why this ant farm is better than others?
1) The ants food and water supply is in the gel. Other ant farms require food and water be added for the ants; adding too much can create mold or too little and the ants are hungry. It’s challenging to calculate and extra work.

2) The glass is fairly narrow front to back so it’s likely the ants (as they did for us) will dig right to the class so you can see them clearly while they work under ground.

3) The light and magnifying glass make it very easy to see every ant at work.

4) The farm is reusable. You can clean out the old gel and ants and buy new ants and gel for a second use.

I highly recommend this gift for any child aged 4-10. Certainly older children and adults will enjoy it too.

LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function I really love these Duplo Lego sets. While I do not have any little ones in the house, I like having some toys on hand for the occasional visitors with kids. These are always a hit and now when friends with little ones come over, the kids always remember our place because of the "Lego Lady!" haha! Bringing out the Legos has brought shy little ones out of their shell as they put together the pieces and play away.

This train set is great! it is super simple to put together, as with any Duplo set. You will need to unscrew the battery box to put in 4 AAA batteries, though. If you're lazy like me and don't want to trudge out to the garage for a screwdriver, you can easily open it with a table knife (haha.. see pic). To make the train go, first be sure there are batteries installed and then push the on/off button on the bottom. put the train on the track. The wheels straddle the inner upright portions of the track (see pic). Then simply give the train a little push and off it goes around the track.

To control the train, use the little action tiles. These are flat pieces with a small icon on them. There is one for each of the following actions. When the train goes over it, it performs the action:
- whistle (yellow) makes a train whistle sound
- horn (white) makes one toot sound - I thought this was for the lights but those didnt come on when it went over this one
- water (blue) stops for a bit there and makes a sound like it is getting water for the steam engine
- reverse (green) stops and reverses the train
- stop (red) stops the train

The action bricks are really easy to put down on the track - they just lay in the middle of the track and don't actually attach. So it is easy for the little ones to pick them up and move them around. This is super fun for the kiddos and definitely keeps them happy occupied for quite some time!

text_fidelity_a:
PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I like the size of the pieces because I have kids in my home who like legos and with those it can be hard to find pieces because they are so small and they end up all over the place. I also like the color combination that was provided. The instructions have to be accessed through a website, which is okay, but I would have liked to have paper directions (but that's just a personal preference).

What I like: 1) within the app it provides step by step directions to build the characters. You have to press play through each step therefore you move along at your own pace. You can also flip the image around so you can see the sides, front, and bottom of the chracter (how it should be) so you can make sure everything is in the right spot. 2) the pieces are very sturdy. I don't forsee myself having a problem with them breaking unless its intentional. 3) it charges really quickly. The block that is the main piece of the entire item is rechargeable. After playing with it for sometime the battery indicated it was on 17% (through the app) and it only took about 20 minutes to fully charge.

What I didn't like: 1) the app is a pain. The description states the item is optimized for android devices with android 7.0 or more, but this is not true. I have three tablets and a samsung chromebook with android 7.0 or more, but when I go to the appstore, it says the app is not optimized for my device or I cannot find the app at all. I had to download the app on my Galaxy S9. Which I would rather the kids be able to play with it on their own devices instead of my phone. I also added it to an iphone XR and it worked. 2) the app isn't the best functionally. It would shut off on me randomly or freeze up. It even caused my phone to go black for about five minutes and after plugging it into the charger and waiting, it finally popped up on camera mode. 3) it is not always easy or fast getting the phone and the item to connect. You have to have your location and bluetooth on and even when the device is powered on, the app will tell you to power it on. Then half the time, it takes 3-5 minutes to finally connect. 4) I like to coding part, because you can do an order of functions, but when you want to just play with it, you can only go back and forth or right and left, depending on the character you built. We built an alligator and it just opened and closed its mouth and not with the same force each time.

Overall, It's a nice toy, but I would not purchase it for $99

Kulipari enemy -“BATTALTIONS” Scorpion Ranger figure with gloved fist and deadly spear! This guy is a solid if not particularly exciting figure. It’s more of a collectible I suppose than a play figure, so I guess if you’re OK with that it serves its purpose.

It’s plastic, with its two claw arms able to pivot at the shoulder a full circle. Nothing else is movable/posable on the body. The plastic feels a bit cheap, and there’s a mold residue on the tail. And the back is stamped with some words and numbers (Mattel, Made in China, etc.).

Again, as a collectible, I suppose it’s fine enough. For play purposes, in our family we strongly recommend figures from Schleich, Pago, or Carnegie, all of which are good sized, nicely detailed, and have an excellent build quality and heft to them. this has a different intent, so I can’t fault it for not meeting those same standards, but that’s just to give some context.

2021 Smart Watches for Women, Fitness Tracker with Blood Pressure Heart Rate Blood Oxygen Monitor, IP68 Waterproof Activity Tracker with Pedometer, Smartwatch for Android Phones I've been on the search for a smartwatch that meets all my needs. I'd like to find one that has a small watch face, bands that can be changed, uses a good app, and can monitor O2, sleep, and a wide variety of exercise. This watch was a perfect 10 in looking nice for my small wrists, and bands that can be changed. Unfortunately it fell quite short of the mark for everything else I needed.

The app has me ready to put this watch back in the box and try something else. It's a really clunky app compared to others I've tried (Fitbit, Da Fit). The exercise feature is very limiting and doesn't account for any indoor exercise like a stationary bike, aerobics, treadmill, etc. Most of the time the steps on the app are wrong compared to the steps on the watch, even after trying to sync it again. It's disappointing that there's so few watch faces to choose from. I can't even choose the screen analog look watch face that is displayed on the box, it's not an option on the app at all. The O2 feature is nice, and so is the sleep feature. I do hope they'll continue to work on the app, it does have potential but doesn't work well for me as it is right now.

I'm also having some trouble trying to use the long press on the watch itself to select features. It's just not working no matter how often I try. It's really disappointing that such a beautiful watch has so many problems. I would have really liked to use it as my main watch, but my search will have to continue on.

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome This is a fun ride-on toy for kids. I like that it sits close to the ground, which makes it better for younger kids, but the design is still “cool” enough that older kids will still like it. The dune buggy has a lot of good features. First, the blue color will appeal to both girls and boys. The vehicle has two speeds, which is nice. However, the parent lock-out needs to be removed to access the higher speed. The lock-out is a screw that’s fairly difficult to remove because of its location. The higher speed is definitely needed to easily ride in the wet grass, even on flat ground. It’s fairly easy to steer the vehicle and is a lot of fun for kids to drive.

To stop the vehicle, take your foot off the gas pedal. It will still slide a little on pavement, possibly because of the plastic wheels. It also will continue to slowly roll going downhill, even on a small incline. That’s why even though the guidelines say ages 3 to 7, I would use caution for younger kids unless you have a large, flat area with no nearby hills. Older kids, up to 11 or 12, will like it, too. However, with the position of the steering wheel, their height will determine how well they’ll comfortably fit in the dune buggy and be able to easily steer.

Be sure to charge the battery the night before using the first time. The battery only lasted about 15 minutes right out of the box after being putting the car together. I also learned the hard way that the dune buggy is heavy to push if it does bog down or if the battery dies. (The battery is rechargeable battery, but there isn’t a battery indicator, so I wasn’t expecting it to go dead so quickly.)

Once the dune buggy is assembled and the battery is charged, it’s a lot of fun for kids. The assembly is a chore for adults, though. I took almost an hour and a half to assemble. Educational Insights Artie 3000 the Coding & Drawing Robot, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 7+ The instructions in the box are lacking and the website is only slightly better. There isn't anything to download to get it to work. It works, the few times it works, via a web browser.

The device itself has a built in WiFi connection. You can, I think, secure it with a password if you want. It's open by default. You connect to it as a WiFi connection then go to its website to get it to work. I find it hangs nearly constantly. Out of the first ten tries, it worked once, each time running the same code. It runs on a very small surface. A sheet of 8 1/2 x 11 printer paper is perfect. It has no edge detection, so mind it doesn't wander off the edge of the table. It starts with the pen fully down by necessity, or at least I can't get it to do anything unless I fully seat the pen, which means it will touch the paper when it is set down,, so it will leave a blob that will bleed through the average paper. Indeed, these bleed almost as bad an an alcohol-based marker.

While it will work with JavaScript or Python, it provides no insight into how to use these languages, so if your kid knows Python they can learn to code the robot in Python, which just means learning its custom library. I would not go so far as to say it teaches much of anything. Hour of code shows as much, is free, and is far more reliable.

It's cute, but until the bugs are worked out, it's not worth the hassle.

text_fidelity_a:
CGE Czech Games Edition Thats A Question Excellent party game from the makers of Codenames. If you've played Codenames, then you know that is a fantastic party game, but that it requires the right group - a slow or domineering player can often mean that everyone is standing around staring at the board for an hour while they dole out perfectly configured clues. It's a fun game, but it requires the right group. That's a Question is a party game that can be played by absolutely anyone, and that, in my opinion, makes it almost a superior game.

In That's a Question!, players use cards to ask A/B style "would you rather" questions in which players attempt to guess the outcome. Based on the results, you move your pawn along the track.

The rulebook is well-written and funny, and is aware that this game is a little bit weird - attempting to give a theme to a basic Q&A style game, but it works. Of course, the game is not perfect. You are limited to only asking three different main questions, although the game does provide a wide variation of answers. There are also point modification questions which allow you to muddy up the scoring in your favor. Ultimately, the scoring was the part of the game that we found most cumbersome, and the modifiers didn't help that, simply adding a little more chaos. Scoring is also modified based on how many players are playing; as this was clearly designed as a 5-6 player game, a 4-player game has a few modifications, and the 3-player game has a fairly substantial number of scoring modifications to make it more challenging. It's nothing you can't figure out, but it is not very clean.

Overall, a good party game for 5-6. The box indicates that this is a game for ages 15+, and nothing in the content of the cards makes me think that anyone from age 7 and up can't handle.
text_fidelity_b: CGE Czech Games Edition Thats A Question

Calm Mindful Puzzle Collection 7-Pack for Relaxation, Stress Relief, and Mood Elevation, for Adults and Kids Ages 8 and up I actually own one of their other single puzzles and really liked it. We do not normally keep puzzles after we do them, but I kept that one. It was a treat to get more of them.

We have now done one of these from our of the package. We did a 500 piece puzzle. It took us about a 24 hour period working on it, stopping, and periodically coming back to it. Not an easy peasy puzzle, but also not one of those frustrating ones. Challenging enough. All the pieces were present and no duplicates.

My only complaint would be, as pictured, the top layer on many pieces peeled in spots. It wasn't just one or two, but quite a handful of them. Not a huge deal, you just press them back down. Could be glued if need be. Just worth mentioning.

Overall. Good, solid, enjoyable puzzle pack. I would not hesitate to buy from this brand. Recommend.
